comment: The table of the trusted boundary of D9.8 and D9.3: the trust bit of a module, which the parser
sets for a first item `import extern;` and the loader sets for a module of a trusted root; the
three errors of a module that is not trusted (a declaration, a call of an extern and a name of a
boundary function, a symbol import included); the precedence of the error of D6.9 at
`rt.args_init`; the walk of the parameter types that finds a boundary function; and the `import
extern;` of the interface writer. The rows cover src/fort/check.ft, parser.ft, modules.ft and
library/interface.ft. Each row breaks one part of the rule. The first stage runs
check_trust_test.ft, which pins each message and position of the checker; the second the corpus
tests of the rule and the D6.9 test fail/stdlib/007; the third the suites of the parser, the
loader, the libraries and D6.9. The table runs in the VM with the debug preset. The md5 guard
reads the product compiler. A row that an earlier run caught stands first, because the first
round of a run in the VM can read stale (notes/testing.md).
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/check.ft && ninja -C build/Linux/debug fort

stages.name: the trust suite
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 6 check_trust_test

stages.name: the trust corpus
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std -j 6 fail/ffi/017 fail/ffi/018 fail/stdlib/007 fail/stdlib/009 fail/stdlib/010 fail/modules/029 fail/modules/030 fail/modules/031 fail/modules/032 run/modules/trusted_types

stages.name: the loader, parser and library suites
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 6 modules_test modules_library_test parser_stmt_test parser_interface_test check_raw_span_test library/interface_test

mutations.what: an `extern fn` of a module that is not trusted is no error
a call of an extern in a module that is not trusted is no error
a call or a value of a boundary function in a module that is not trusted is no error
a symbol import of a boundary function is no error
a symbol import of `rt.args_init` gets the error of D9.8 and not that of D6.9

mutations.new:
report_boundary_name(ck, s, n->name_loc);
            check_error(ck, n->name_loc, ARGS_INIT_ERROR);

the walk reads no result of a function pointer type
the walk reads no field of a struct
a walk that found a byte pointer keeps its structs as reaching none
the walk reads the fields of a struct in error
